'''Puttu''' is a [[Cookbook:breakfast|breakfast]] dish in Kerala, India. The main ingredients are rice [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] and coconut. It is usually eaten with [[Cookbook:Steaming|steamed]] bananas or [[Cookbook:Cholley|Kadala Curry]] ([[Cookbook:Chickpea|chickpea]] curry), [[Cookbook:Chicken Curry|Chicken Curry]], or [[Cookbook:Boil|boiled]] green gram ([[Cookbook:Mung Bean|moong]]) and pappad.
== Ingredients==
* 1 medium-sized [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]]
* 4 cups puttu powder ([[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook: Water|Water]] (enough to moisten the flour)

== Procedure == 

#[[Cookbook:Grating|Grate]] the coconut flesh finely.
#Mix the puttu powder and salt in a wide bowl. Add half of the grated coconut.
#Rub the mixture with your fingertips, sprinkling in water until it is moist and develops a coarse texture.
#Leave the mixture for an hour if the flour is ready made, as it absorbs more water.
#Check the consistency of the flour. One should be able to make a ball out of the flour that can be easily crumbled. Adjust the water content accordingly.
#Spread a little coconut over the bottom of the puttu vessel (''puttu kutti''), and fill it with the moist flour. Layer it with coconut.
#Steam it on the puttu vessel or on the pressure cooker nozzle. In a few minutes, steam will start escaping through the top of the puttu vessel. It will be done in 4 minutes.
#Serve hot with kadala curry, boiled green gram and pappad (payarum pappadavum), or with steamed bananas.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]], [[Cookbook:wheat|wheat]], [[Cookbook:corn|corn]], ragi, or [[Cookbook:tapioca|tapioca]] flours can all be used to make puttu.
